design.concept: Decision-first board: the pending expenses are a grid of cards, each opened by a full-width status strip and showing who, how much and when at a glance. Opening a card takes the manager to the expense panel, where the outcomes (Approve / Reject with the reason right below) come first and the facts follow underneath. The decision is one glance and one click.

views.purpose: The board of pending expenses with loading, error and empty states, and a load-more control.
The panel of the chosen expense: identity line, outcome buttons and rejection reason at the top, then the facts. It replaces the board as its own scene, with a back control.

design.decisions: Followed the decisionFirst template, not the section order of the defs: no table and no side-by-side split. The queue is a card grid (3 columns on wide desktop, 2 on narrow), and each card starts with a status band that uses the status tokens. The detail is its own scene through the scene host, because views may only switch there. Back clears the selection. In the panel, the identity line and the outcomes (decisaoDespesa) come before the facts (analiseDespesa). The rejection reason is always present under the buttons, since the page cannot hold state to open it, and its required error shows in plain words. After a decision, the outcome row is replaced by one line saying what was decided and the panel stays open. Failures show right above the buttons. Search, period filter and the receipt viewer were left out: the shared has no filter state and the rows have no receipt field. The empty board has a large icon, one sentence and a reload action. Status words, labels and wording come from the L4 titles.
